notes: Only the VAT part of the 20% is reclaimable, and this release corrects that. Ghana's 20% on an invoice is three taxes — VAT at 15%, the NHIL at 2.5% and the GETFund levy at 2.5% — and only the VAT is deductible input tax; the two levies are a cost of whatever was bought. The app treated the whole 20% as reclaimable whenever the organisation was VAT-registered, so on a GHS 1,000 purchase it claimed 200 where 150 was due: the business under-paid the GRA by 50 and understated its own expenses by the same 50, on every purchase. IF YOU ARE NOT VAT-REGISTERED NOTHING ABOUT YOUR BOOKS CHANGES — no input-VAT line was ever written for you, so there was nothing to over-claim. Now: a payment or vendor bill reclaims only the VAT component and the levies go into the expense; a debit note reverses only what was actually claimed (it used to credit the whole VAT back, driving the input-VAT account negative); on a payment split across several expense heads the non-reclaimable levy is charged to the line that bore the VAT, so zero-rated goods beside standard-rated services no longer absorb part of the services line's levies; and the reclaimable share is a rate — VAT_RECOVERABLE, seeded at 15 — under Settings, Tax rates, so it follows a budget without waiting for a release. The VAT Return now says why input VAT is less than the whole charge. Nothing to do on upgrade: existing entries are untouched, this changes how new ones post. If you are VAT-registered and have been reclaiming, your accountant will want to know the input-VAT account was overstated before this version.
